Chapter 9: Navigating Change and Uncertainty With the Unconscious Mind
Let’s be honest—change never really feels comfortable, does it? Even when we choose it, suddenly old fears and doubts seem to bubble up. That’s what this chapter is all about: how we handle those moments when life shifts beneath our feet.
Think about a man who’s just retired after decades on the job. His work was a huge part of who he was. Now, every day feels wide open—and instead of freedom, he feels lost. Old anxieties start creeping in—he wonders if he still matters, or what his future holds. At first, he tries to keep busy, filling his days with activities, but nothing seems to fit.
Little by little, though, he starts tuning in to those quieter voices inside—the need for connection, a spark of creativity, maybe even just a longing for some rest. He takes up volunteering, dusts off his old paints, and calls up friends he hasn’t seen in years. The transition isn’t smooth or easy, but it becomes a time where unexpected growth takes root.
Here’s something to pay attention to: our unconscious mind is wired to crave safety and predictability. So when our routines get knocked out of place, it’s totally normal to feel anxious, sad, or even angry. These emotions aren’t weaknesses—they’re just signals that our mind is working hard to adjust to something new.
One powerful way to navigate change is to honor that discomfort, instead of fighting or ignoring it. When we acknowledge the fear or grief that comes up, it’s like we’re giving ourselves permission to move through it, rather than getting stuck. With a little time and compassion, our unconscious mind really can adapt.
Tools like visualization and mindfulness come in handy here, too. When you picture a positive outcome, or simply stay present with what’s happening right now, it’s like you’re telling your mind, “Hey, it’s okay to relax. We can handle this.” That creates space for new ideas, and opens the door to fresh possibilities.
Picture a young woman going through the end of a relationship. She’s overwhelmed by sadness and regret, and at first she tries to distract herself, hoping the feelings will just fade. But they don’t. Eventually, she lets herself grieve—writing in her journal, talking with friends, really feeling those emotions. Over time, she notices something shift. There’s still pain, but now there’s a glimmer of hope—a curiosity about what comes next. That pain doesn’t vanish, but it becomes just one part of a bigger story of resilience and growth.
So, here’s the key takeaway: change is always going to be part of life, but suffering doesn’t have to be. If we listen to our unconscious mind—respecting its fears, honoring its wisdom, and gently guiding it forward—we can move through life’s transitions with so much more ease and grace.
